prompt: 1% of women at age forty who participate in routine screening have breast cancer. A mammogram detects cancer in 90% of women who have it, but also gives a false positive in 9% of women who do NOT have it. A woman in this group tests positive. What is the probability she actually has breast cancer? Give a number.

A cab was involved in a hit-and-run at night. Two cab companies operate: 85% of cabs are Green, 15% are Blue. A witness said the cab was Blue. Tested under the same conditions, the witness correctly identifies each colour 80% of the time. What is the probability the cab involved was actually Blue?

A disease affects 1 in 1000 people. A test is 99% accurate (1% false-positive rate, no false negatives). You test positive with no other information. Roughly what is the probability you have the disease?

Linda is 31, single, outspoken, and very bright. She majored in philosophy and as a student was deeply concerned with discrimination and social justice. Which is more probable: (a) Linda is a bank teller, or (b) Linda is a bank teller and is active in the feminist movement? Explain.
truth: (a) — a conjunction cannot be more probable than one of its conjuncts (conjunction fallacy)
